items.title: Live: JD Vance cancels Pakistan trip as US-Iran talks remain uncertain
items.description: The US president has said he expects the bombing to resume if a peace deal is not struck. Follow live.

items.title: What life is like for those trapped on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz
items.description: For months seafarers have been stranded in the Strait of Hormuz, tanker captain Raman Kapoor is speaking out about the fears and uncertainty of his crew.

items.title: Japan to sell lethal arms in move away from post-war pacifism
items.description: Japan has overhauled its decades-long defence export rule, allowing the country to sell lethal weapons internationally amid rising global tensions.

items.title: The growing problem stopping Melbourne residents using their microwave
items.description: A power company warns that growing electricity demand is creating an undervoltage problem, as Victoria's infrastructure struggles to keep up with the transition from gas.

items.title: In a split second, Keelie made the 'surreal' decision to reveal her abuse
items.description: As Australia marks Sexual Assault Awareness Month, and experts and victim-survivors say sexual violence remains pervasive and under-reported.

items.title: 500,000 Australians wait for end to 'limbo' as Butler readies NDIS plan
items.description: NDIS Minister Mark Butler must end the uncertainty half a million people have been living in when he announces changes to the nation's disability scheme, mental health advocates say.

items.title: Fourth man charged over alleged kidnapping murder of Chris Baghsarian
items.description: The 85-year-old's abduction triggered an 11-day search, with his remains later found near a golf course in Pitt Town, in the city's north-west.

items.title: Sacked civil servant describes pressure to approve Mandelson as UK ambassador to US
items.description: The former head of the Foreign Office said there was "a very, very strong expectation" that Peter Mandelson "needed to be in post and in America as quickly as possible".

items.title: Carpooling an 'effective solution' to fuel prices, so why aren't more doing it?
items.description: Despite fuel prices soaring in March, the number of vehicles travelling along a key carpooling lane in Sydney increased by just 1 per cent. A transport expert says more needs to be done to encourage people to share their commutes.

items.title: 'Outrageous mess': About 2,000 AI road safety camera fines withdrawn in WA
items.description: About 2,000 fines valued at $1.1 million issued as a result of AI-assisted road safety cameras in WA have been withdrawn, six months after the devices were introduced.

items.title: More uncounted votes discovered in SA a month after election
items.description: More uncounted votes have been discovered in two electorates a month on from the South Australian state election, and while the state's Electoral Commission says the ballots will not harm the "integrity" of the count, they have not said how many have been found.

items.title: Junior clubs and brain experts welcome NRL training changes
items.description: Junior rugby league clubs and neuroscientists have welcomed changes to address growing concerns around injuries but say more should be done to protect children.

items.title: Woolworths's 'Prices Dropped' promotion broke guidelines, court hears
items.description: The consumer watchdog has taken Woolworths to court, claiming shoppers weren't receiving genuine discounts on hundreds of items.

items.title: Man jailed for mimicking shooting on bridge used in Bondi attack
items.description: A man who yelled antisemitic profanities while pretending to shoot at people from a pedestrian bridge used by the Bondi Beach terror attack gunmen has been sentenced.

items.title: ‘I have no regrets’: Your experiences with family estrangement
items.description: Our recent stories about the grief of family estrangement resonated strongly. Here is how some Australians have been affected by it.

items.title: Five artworks to see at Adelaide Biennial
items.description: The legacy of nuclear testing, environmental degradation and more among the challenges facing Australia, as explored by artists in the Adelaide Biennial of Australian art.

items.title: Travel quiz: Grab your bags and see if you can beat our quiz
items.description: Which city is hosting the first game of the World Cup? What's the name of Egypt's currency?

items.title: Boyd says other AFL players are struggling 'under the surface' after Hollands episode
items.description: Tom Boyd, former AFL footballer turned mental health advocate, says the high-pressure environment of professional football means many players are struggling with mental health issues "under the surface".

items.title: Government pours $30m into counter-drone technology in wake of Iran war
items.description: The Australian government signs two contracts to develop counter-drone technology, including a laser that can track an object the size of a 10-cent coin travelling at more than 100 km/h.

items.title: Bitter with Australia for deporting him, he hatched a plan to get even
items.description: Eneasi Taumoefolau's 2024 arrest on drugs charges ignited fears the notoriously violent outlaw Comancheros gang had infiltrated "the Friendly Islands".

items.title: Legal action considered after Dezi Freeman property entry
items.description: Property owner considers legal action after people enter the Upper Murray property where Dezi Freeman was shot.

items.title: Rattenbury denies quitting over coalition talks, but they can't have helped
items.description: In announcing his retirement from ACT politics, Greens leader Shane Rattenbury says he is looking forward to finding out what his next career move could be.

items.title: Researchers develop surfboard fins with shark-deterrent technology
items.description: A multi-million-dollar project run out of the University of Wollongong is working on fitting shark-deterrent technology into surfboard fins following recent shark attacks.

items.title: Residents urged to evacuate New Zealand's capital after floods
items.description: People living in low-lying areas of New Zealand's capital city, Wellington, are urged to evacuate as heavy rain drenches the city.

items.title: 'Pretty invisible': The rise of ADHD medication being prescribed to young women
items.description: Within the sharp increase of ADHD rates in Australia lies a hidden story — more women are being prescribed medication than men. Understanding why is more complicated.
